conditions: There is a project called "Aurora" in the workspace.
Aurora has a milestone whose due date is September 30 (year unspecified, presumed the relevant/only matching one).
That milestone is "still-unstarted" — no work under it has progressed yet.
Under that specific milestone, there is an issue whose assignee is Priya Nair.
That issue is the only one meeting the assignee condition (the phrasing "the issue" presumes uniqueness).
The action to perform: set that issue's priority field to Urgent.

readings: No issue under the milestone has moved past Backlog/Todo (progress-based, inferred from its issues' statuses).
The milestone's due date simply hasn't arrived yet / it hasn't formally begun (calendar-based), independent of issue progress.
The nearest/only milestone due Sept 30 regardless of year.
Specifically an upcoming Sept 30 (e.g., 2026) if multiple milestones with that due date across different years exist.

turn2.differences: The author's two conditions (c1: assignee, c2: Aurora's still-unstarted milestone due Sept 30) collapse what I broke into finer pieces in step 1 (project=Aurora, milestone due date, milestone status, and issue-under-that-milestone) but carry the same substance. The implicit uniqueness requirement ('the issue') isn't stated as a separate condition, but it's satisfied incidentally: although Priya Nair is assigned to four issues total, only i-target also satisfies c2, so the combined conditions pick out a unique record even without an explicit uniqueness clause.

ambiguity_effects.explain: A looser, progress-based reading (progress == 0 means 'unstarted') would also pull in i-decoy-status, since its milestone has progress 0.0. But the data gives milestones an explicit status field, and 'still-unstarted' most naturally maps to the literal value 'unstarted', which m-status-decoy's status ('next') does not match. A careful reader anchoring on the literal field label would not remain unsure - they'd exclude it - though a less careful colleague could contest it, which is why I marked that record contestable rather than calling it a live ambiguity.
All Sept 30 milestones in the data are dated 2026, so the unstated year doesn't actually create competing candidates here; the ambiguity is moot given these records.

ambiguity_effects.explain: Priya Nair is assigned to four issues, so this phrase alone doesn't pick a unique one, but combined with c2 (Aurora's still-unstarted milestone due Sept 30) only i-target remains. The uniqueness presumption in 'the issue' turns out to hold once both conditions are applied together.

turn2.naturalness_note: The phrasing reads like a plausible request from someone who works with Linear milestones regularly (referencing a project name, a milestone's due date, and its not-yet-started status together) - it doesn't contain telltale synthetic-test markers like exposed IDs or overly exhaustive qualifiers.
